newsitem.title: USA: CBOT disputes CFTC on listing 1999 corn/soy months.
newsitem.headline: CBOT disputes CFTC on listing 1999 corn/soy months.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade sharply disputed a statement by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) that the exchange had acted without legal authority in listing its new 1999 corn and soybean contracts.

The contracts, listed on April 25 under new delivery terms not yet approved by the CFTC, had been clearly described as still subject to approval by CFTC, CBOT President Patrick Arbor said in a statement.

"The exchange listed trading months that had long been part of a trading months cycle pre-approved by the CFTC," Arbor said, adding that the 1999 contracts would normally have been listed no later than December, 1996.
Arbor said the CFTC had also been told in advance by the CBOT of the plan to go ahead with the listing.

On Friday, May 2, CFTC sent a letter to the exchange stating that the listing of the 1999 contracts was "not legally authorized at the present time" and told the CBOT to notify all market participants to that effect immediately.

"By return correspondence, the exchange has disputed the commission's assertion that these contract months are not legally authorized," Arbor said. "In the exchange's view, such an assertion has no statutory or other basis and represents a sharp departure from past practice.

"Moreover, by failing to object in a timely fashion to our expressed intention to list these contract months and by belatedly sending this notification to the exchange, the Commission is needlessly exposing market participants to significant legal and market uncertainty," Arbor said.

The contracts in question are the July and December 1999 corn contracts and July and November 1999 soybean contracts. They include provisions to drop Toledo as a delivery point and change to Illinois River locations, a plan CFTC is reviewing.

"The commission hereby instructs the CBT that it must notify all market participants that the Commission has not approved the listing of these contract months as required by law, that the Commission may approve or disapprove the listing of these contract months, and that the Commission may approve, disapprove, supplement or modify the delivery terms applicable to these trading months," the CFTC letter to the CBOT said.
